mageHello1.say: Another Vestige from the sea? Show me. I never tire of these.

mageHello2.say: The sea gives things up when it chooses. Let us see what it chose.

mageHello3.say: Each one is sealed a little differently. I would love to know why.

mageThanks1.say: There. Not what I expected. They never are.

mageThanks2.say: Opened. Strange, what the water keeps for us.

armorsmithHello1.say: Armour. Good steel, fitted here. Pick one or stand aside.

armorsmithHello2.say: New plate today. Better than whatever the sea throws at you.

armorsmithHello3.say: Wear it, do not admire it. Nothing out there cares how it looks.

armorsmithThanks1.say: It will hold. Mind the straps.

armorsmithThanks2.say: Good. Come back with it dented.

armorsmithShort1.say: Not enough Aurem. Steel is not cheap in Overlook.

weaponsmithHello1.say: Blades, bows, guns. Something sharp for whatever the sea sends.

weaponsmithHello2.say: The Grey Tithe took their tenth again, I hear. Take something that bites back.

weaponsmithHello3.say: Every one of these is tested. Mostly on driftwood.

weaponsmithThanks1.say: Keep it oiled. Salt eats everything.

weaponsmithThanks2.say: Good. Now go and use it.

weaponsmithShort1.say: Not enough. I do not haggle.

tailorHello1.say: Ah, someone who cares how they look. Rare, in Overlook.

tailorHello2.say: I mix every colour by my own hand. Nobody else here bothers.

tailorHello3.say: Salt fades everything. My dyes fade last. Ask anyone worth asking.

tailorThanks1.say: You will be the best dressed on the harbour. After me.

tailorThanks2.say: Wear it well. People will ask where you found it.

tailorShort1.say: Beauty costs, I am afraid. More than you carry.

tackHello1.say: Bring your horse round sometime. I have something for every coat.

tackHello2.say: Horses hate the salt as much as we do. Be kind to yours.

tackHello3.say: Good barding keeps the spray off. A pretty one keeps their spirits up.

tackThanks1.say: Your horse will thank you. Mine always do.

tackThanks2.say: Lovely. Give them an apple from me.

tackShort1.say: Not quite enough, love. The horse can wait a day.

stormcallerHello1.say: Quick now. What do you need? The weather is turning.

stormcallerHello2.say: You look like someone who hates standing still. Good.

stormcallerHello3.say: The storm does not wait. Neither do we.

stormcallerThanks1.say: Done. Go, before the wind changes.

stormcallerShort1.say: Not enough. Come back quicker, and with more.

marenHello1.say: Sit a while, child. The lamps will keep.

marenHello2.say: Three ports still stand. We keep our lamps lit all the same.

marenHello3.say: Overlook remembers things its own way. I remember them slowly.

marenThanks1.say: There. May it light your way home.

marenThanks2.say: Look after it, and it will outlast us both.

marenShort1.say: Not yet, dear. Come back when you can. I will be here.

shapeHello1.say: You came. The sea said you would.

shapeHello3.say: I was here before. You do not remember. No one does.
